hook_text: A beetle that drinks fog, a plant that lives for centuries on two leaves, and a bird that carries water in its feathers. How?
clip_script: A nature reserve near Springbok. Fat succulent leaves full of water. A quiver tree with a white, shiny trunk that reflects the sun. Tiny stone plants hiding from the heat. In the Namib, a welwitschia grows only two long leaves for its whole life. A fennec fox loses heat through its huge ears. A sandgrouse soaks its belly feathers to carry water to its chicks. Every desert living thing has a trick for saving water.
visual_style: Whiteboard desert scene with labelled plants storing water, roots spreading wide and deep, and animals in burrows, with arrows showing water being saved.
mood: Curious and clever, like discovering secret survival tricks.
pacing: One plant or animal at a time, each with its special trick.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and design your own imaginary desert animal with three adaptations.
